newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland against five-power European security summit.
newsitem.headline: Poland against five-power European security summit.

text.p: Poland, a leading candidate for early NATO membership, on Thursday criticised a proposal to hold a five-power summit on European security ahead of the alliance's expansion.

"This is an unfortunate idea," foreign ministry spokesman Pawel Dobrowolski told Reuters. "From the Polish point of view, it would be an unnecessary element of the process (expansion), which is already well shaped."
"It is an initiative which could be applauded by opponents of our accession plans," he added.

Russia, which opposes NATO's plan to recruit new members from Eastern Europe, said on Thursday it was ready to take part in such a summit, though a frosty U.S. response to the idea cast doubts on whether it could go ahead.

Both French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl have visited Russia this year and diplomats said on Wednesday that they had backed the idea of a security summit, suggested for April.

The five-power meeting, involving the United States, Britain, France and Germany, would allow Russia to discuss NATO plans to expand eastwards before NATO holds its own decisive summit on the issue on July 8 and 9 in Madrid.
But Dobrowolski said such a meeting could disturb the process of NATO enlargement which had already been agreed.
NATO has said it will invite the first former members of the defunct Soviet-led Warsaw Pact for talks on membership during its Madrid summit.
Poland, which escaped Moscow's domination in 1989, is a front-runner along with the Czech Republic and Hungary.
